title: Platform Systems & Services: Playbook, How-tos, Dashboards, Runbooks, Roadmap, and Team Wiki
author: Liam Chen
content:
Overview

This page is the canonical team wiki for Platform Systems & Services: it consolidates operational runbooks, dashboard and alerting standards, platform how-tos, postmortem retrospectives, and the near-term roadmap. The goal is to provide a single place for engineers and on-call responders to find instructions, ownership, thresholds, and escalation paths for common platform incidents and routine operations.

Scope

- Services covered: routing-proxy, request-router, runtime-autoscaler, cache-service, model-mesh, metrics-collector, alert-bridge.
- Environments: prod-us, prod-eu, staging, qa.
- Audience: platform engineers, SRE, on-call, infra, and product engineers who operate or depend on platform services.

Table of contents

1) How-tos and standard operating procedures
2) Dashboards and alerting 
3) Runbooks (by incident class)
4) Retrospectives and continuous improvements
5) Roadmap (quarterly priorities)
6) Team wiki and contacts

1) How-tos and standard operating procedures

Intro: The following how-tos are step-by-step procedures used for routine tasks and emergency interventions. Follow the numbered checks, and escalate if the issue is not resolved within the expected timeline.

A. Deploying a platform service (canary -> full rollout)

1. Create a PR against infra/helm-charts with a single commit that updates image tag and chart values. Include changelog and risk assessment.
2. Run pipeline: ci/cd -> integration tests -> canary deploy to prod-us/canary namespace.
3. Verify: smoke tests, perf smoke (p95 tail latency < baseline), and dashboard health (error rate < 0.1%).
4. Wait 30 minutes for autoscaling stability and KV cache warm-up.
5. If stable, promote to 20% traffic for 1 hour, then 100% if metrics are green.
6. If any step fails, follow the rollback procedure (see B).

B. Rollback procedure (service-level rollback)

1. Trigger rollback via CI: revert image tag to previous release and re-run pipeline.
2. If immediate rollback required (service is causing >1% error rate or impacting SLOs): scale new replicas to 0 using kubectl scale/patch and restore previous deployment image. Notify #platform-ops and on-call.
3. Open an incident in PagerDuty and assign to platform on-call. Post links to incident channel.

C. Adding a dashboard panel (Grafana)

1. Create a feature branch in observability/dashboards and add a panel JSON. Panels must include: title, metric query, unit, default threshold lines, and a short owner note.
2. Submit PR with screenshot and rationale. Include expected alert thresholds if appropriate.
3. Approval by owner + one reviewer. Merge triggers automation to publish the dashboard.

D. Adding a new alert rule (Prometheus Alertmanager)

1. Define alert name, description, severity (sev1/sev2/sev3), owner, and runbook link.
2. Use templated rule format: expr, for, labels (team, severity), annotations (summary, runbook_url).
3. Run lint and dry-run in staging.
4. Notify reviewers and schedule activation during low-traffic window for production.

2) Dashboards and alerting

Standard dashboards (owners):
- Platform Overview (owner: platform-observability) — high-level SLOs, request QPS, global error rate, regional latency heatmap.
- Request Router Health (owner: runtime-team) — p50/p90/p99 latencies, active connections, queue depth.
- GPU Fleet Utilization (owner: infra-gpu) — per-pool utilization, memory pressure, OOM events.
- Model Mesh & KV Cache (owner: model-serving) — cache hit rate, cold-start rate, average KV size.
- Cost & Throttling (owner: cost-ops) — request cost per token, throttled requests, rate-limiter metrics.

Alerting policy (summary):
- Sev1 (PagerDuty): platform SLO breach (95% success; >5 minutes sustained), region down (all routing nodes unhealthy), or complete autoscaler failure.
- Sev2 (Slack + Email): degraded performance (p99 latency > 3x baseline for 15 minutes), sustained error rate > 1% for 30 minutes.
- Sev3 (Email + Ticket): non-urgent increases in cache misses, minor API error spikes, and infra warnings.

Example alert rule (text form):
- alert: PlatformRequestErrorRateHigh
  expr: sum(rate(requests_total{job="request-router",status!~"2.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(requests_total{job="request-router"}[5m])) > 0.01
  for: 15m
  labels: {team: "platform-runner", severity: "sev2"}
  annotations: {summary: "Request router error rate >1% for 15m", runbook_url: "https://confluence/internal/runbooks/platform-request-errors"}

3) Runbooks (by incident class)

A. Route-level outage (partial or full region) — Sev1

- Detection: PagerDuty alert: RegionRoutingDown OR PlatformRequestErrorRateHigh with region tag.
- Immediate actions (first 10 minutes):
  1) Acknowledge PagerDuty. Post incident banner in #platform-incident.
  2) Triage: check region nodes (kubectl get pods -n routing), control-plane logs, and LB health in cloud console.
  3) If control-plane unreachable, activate cross-region failover as documented in "routing-failover-howto".
- If failover executed: verify traffic redistribution, check p99 latency, and watch for cascading rate limiting.
- Post-incident: run RCA using standard template and publish to confluence within 72 hours.

B. High tail latency on runtime (sev2 -> sev1 if impacts SLO)

- Detection: p99 > baseline * 3 for 15 minutes.
- Actions:
  1) Scale up runtime-autoscaler pool (k8s HPA or node pool) and capture heap/profile traces.
  2) Toggle batching config to smaller batch sizes: /api/v1/configs/batching -> set max_batch_tokens to baseline.
  3) If latency persists, roll back latest runtime release.

C. GPU OOM or memory pressure (sev2)

- Detection: GPU OOM events in metrics-collector or node-exporter logs.
- Actions: cordon affected nodes, migrate active pods to healthy capacity, drain node for diagnostics. Open infra ticket and notify infra-gpu team.

4) Retrospectives and continuous improvements

Process: Every Sev1 incident triggers a retro. Owner (incident commander) must schedule the retro within 5 business days. Retro deliverables:
- Timeline and impact summary
- Root cause and contributing factors
- Action items with owners and due dates (tracked in JIRA)
- Verification plan for each action (how we will measure success)

Example improvements from past retros:
- Q4 2025: Reduced cold-start tail latency by 40% by implementing a warm-start pool for high-traffic model variants.
- Q1 2026: Introduced per-route cost breakdowns in dashboards which identified a misconfigured reranking route consuming 3x expected tokens.

5) Roadmap (next 3 quarters)

2026-Q2 (near term)
- Platform observability: roll out per-route SLO dashboards and route-level anomaly detection.
- Autoscaler: introduce predictive autoscaling prototype for model-mesh workloads.
- Playbook consolidation: merge all service-level runbooks into a single searchable playbook index.

2026-Q3
- Fast-fail fallbacks: automatic model-variant fallback when quantized variant fails more than 5% of requests.
- GPU pool defragmentation tooling: reduce fragmentation by live migration heuristics.
- Cost optimizations: automated batching recommendations surfaced in console.

2026-Q4 and beyond
- Private deployment observability parity: get on-prem agents to ship full SLO telemetry.
- Cross-region circuit breaker and dynamic routing policies for cost/latency tradeoffs.

6) Team wiki and contacts

Primary contacts and responsibilities:
- Platform On-call (rotation): see rota in PagerDuty team: platform-oncall.
- Platform Observability (owner): Ava Moreno (ava@redwood.ai).
- Infra GPU (owner): Diego Alvarez (diego@redwood.ai).
- Runtime Team Lead: Priya Kapoor (priya@redwood.ai).

Useful links:
- Observability repo: https://git.internal/redwood/observability
- Dashboards landing: https://grafana.internal/d/platform-overview
- Runbook index: https://confluence/internal/eng-platform/runbooks-index

Appendix: Maintenance checklist (monthly)

- Review active alerts and tune thresholds where >10% false positive rate.
- Verify dashboard ownership and update contact info.
- Run canary traffic test for failover procedures (document result).
- Audit autoscaler policies for under/over-provisioning.

If you have updates to this page, follow the page edit guidelines: include rationale, test evidence, and a reviewer from observability. For Sev1 runbook changes, require at least one SRE and one runtime engineer sign-off before merging.
